_comment: CRuby -> mruby API map for convert_mrbgem.rb. kind: call (rename; inject mrb as first arg when inject_mrb), macro (rename or identity, no mrb), expr (identifier replaced by an expression), type (identifier replaced), special (handled by converter code), refuse (no equivalent; marker left in output). needs_mrb marks identifiers that require an mrb_state in scope. Any CRuby-looking identifier missing from this file is refused by the converter.

type_check_refused._comment: Check_Type and rb_check_type (handler check_type in convert_mrbgem.rb) map a T_ name only when its entry has type_check exact or caveat. These names are refused with the reason given here.
type_check_refused.T_OBJECT: mruby's MRB_TT_OBJECT does not match CRuby's T_OBJECT: CRuby allocates exceptions as T_OBJECT (ruby4src error.c:3583 via object.c:118), mruby allocates them as MRB_TT_EXCEPTION (src/error.c:42), so the check would reject exceptions
type_check_refused.T_CLASS: mruby's MRB_TT_CLASS does not match CRuby's T_CLASS: a CRuby singleton class is a class with RUBY_FL_SINGLETON (ruby4src class.c:42), mruby allocates singleton classes as MRB_TT_SCLASS (src/class.c:371), so the check would reject them
type_check_refused.T_FIXNUM: mruby has one integer tag, MRB_TT_FIXNUM (include/mruby/value.h:109); CRuby's Fixnum/Bignum split is not mruby's integer range, so MRB_TT_FIXNUM matches every Integer (see the RB_TYPE_P caveat)
type_check_refused.T_BIGNUM: stuck point: the fork has no Bignum. No MRB_TT_BIGINT tag exists (include/mruby/value.h:106-131) and no mrbgem defines a big-integer class, so no tag or class test can select CRuby's T_BIGNUM values
type_check_refused.T_NIL: nil and false share mruby's tag MRB_TT_FALSE (include/mruby/value.h:106, MRB_TT_FALSE; mrb_nil_p tells them apart by value, value.h:184), so a type check cannot tell nil from false
type_check_refused.T_FALSE: mruby's MRB_TT_FALSE (include/mruby/value.h:106) also matches nil, which CRuby reports as T_NIL
type_check_refused.T_TRUE: not in the type-check subset of this change (refused as listed); mruby's MRB_TT_TRUE (include/mruby/value.h:107) is true only, so it can be added as its own change
type_check_refused.T_UNDEF: CRuby's Qundef is an internal marker, not a Ruby object type; mruby's MRB_TT_UNDEF (value.h:111) is a separate value kind
type_check_refused.T_STRUCT: the fork has no MRB_TT_STRUCT tag (include/mruby/value.h:106-131); Struct instances are an mrbgem class (mrbgems/mruby-struct), so a type test would be a class test, which is not made here
type_check_refused.T_REGEXP: stuck point: the fork has no Regexp tag (include/mruby/value.h:106-131) and no mrbgem defines a Regexp class (mrbgems/ lists no mruby-regexp), so there is nothing to compare with
type_check_refused.T_RATIONAL: the fork has no MRB_TT_RATIONAL tag: Rational is the mruby-rational mrbgem class (mrbgems/mruby-rational), so a test is mrb_obj_is_kind_of against it. Where the state is in scope RB_TYPE_P converts to that test; a case label of a switch cannot test a class, so a switch on T_RATIONAL needs an if-chain (not made here); Check_Type in a function without the state is refused
type_check_refused.T_COMPLEX: the fork has no MRB_TT_COMPLEX tag; Complex is the mruby-complex mrbgem class (mrbgems/mruby-complex), so a type test is a class test against that gem, which is not made here

unmapped_reasons._comment: A name with no api_map entry is refused with the reason given here (the converter's no-entry path). PRIsVALUE is converted where rb_raise and rb_sprintf take it; elsewhere it is an argument of rb_enc_sprintf, which takes an rb_encoding *.
unmapped_reasons.PRIsVALUE: stuck point (Encoding): PRIsVALUE outside rb_raise and rb_sprintf is an argument of rb_enc_sprintf, which takes an rb_encoding *; the fork has no Encoding (accepted stuck point)

Data_Make_Struct.caveat: a static mrb_data_type per call with the mark and free callbacks (threaded); the struct is zeroed

rb_const_get_at.caveat: the receiver's own constant table only (the fork's mrb_const_get_at, branch claude/const-get-at); a missing constant goes to const_missing, which raises NameError, as in CRuby. The receiver must be a tracked class or a mapped class constant

NUM2INT.caveat: NUM2INT converts through mruby's integer conversion (mrb_to_int, the mrb_int macro): a Float is truncated, a non-numeric value raises TypeError

NUM2LONG.caveat: NUM2LONG converts through mruby's integer conversion (mrb_to_int, the mrb_int macro): a Float is truncated, a non-numeric value raises TypeError

INT2NUM.caveat: mruby's Integer (mrb_fixnum_value); the value is converted to mrb_int

LONG2NUM.caveat: mruby's Integer (mrb_fixnum_value); the value is converted to mrb_int

rb_streql_lit.caveat: the second argument is a string literal, made a mruby String; mrb_str_equal compares the bytes, as CRuby's rb_streql_lit (length and memcmp)

rb_ensure.caveat: both callbacks are static VALUE f(VALUE) functions of this file used only here; they take (mrb, value) after threading, and mrb_ensure runs the ensure callback before re-raising an exception, as CRuby does

rb_rescue.reason: no direct mruby equivalent (rescue callback not in the supported subset)

rb_rescue2.reason: no direct mruby equivalent (rescue callback not in the supported subset)

rb_gc_register_address.caveat: needs the mruby fork's address roots (claude/gc-address-roots: mrb_gc_register_address reads *ptr at each collection); the value at the address stays rooted for as long as it is registered

rb_gc_register_mark_object.caveat: mrb_gc_register keeps the value in mruby's root table (src/gc.c:564) for the life of the state; CRuby never unregisters it either. Immediate values need no root and are ignored by mrb_gc_register

rb_gc_mark.caveat: valid only inside a data type mark callback (the runtime passes the state); refused elsewhere

rb_gc_mark_movable.caveat: valid only inside a data type mark callback, as rb_gc_mark; mruby does not compact, so a movable mark is the same mark (the mark hook is the fork's mrb_data_type.mark, branch claude/markable-data-type)

rb_gc_enable.reason: no mruby enable function: gc.disabled is a VM flag (include/mruby/gc.h), and CRuby's return value (the previous state) would have to be emulated

rb_gc_disable.reason: no mruby disable function: gc.disabled is a VM flag (include/mruby/gc.h), and CRuby's return value (the previous state) would have to be emulated

StringValuePtr.caveat: the argument is converted in place with to_str; the argument must be a plain identifier

StringValueCStr.caveat: argument must already be a String: no to_str conversion and no NUL-byte check

NUM2ULONG.caveat: NUM2ULONG converts through mruby's integer conversion (mrb_to_int, the mrb_int macro): a Float is truncated, a non-numeric value raises TypeError

rb_str_new_frozen.caveat: returns a copy; the copy is not frozen

rb_thread_call_without_gvl.caveat: modelled on mruby-uv: func runs on the libuv thread pool and the caller runs the loop until it finishes; ubf is ignored (no interrupt)

rb_ext_ractor_safe.reason: ractor declaration; mruby has no ractors, so the declaration has no effect

rb_ary_pop.caveat: returns the last element, or nil for an empty array, as CRuby does

rb_str_subseq.caveat: returns a new String of len bytes from beg; mruby strings carry no encoding, so the result is not re-encoded

rb_intern3.caveat: the encoding argument is dropped: mruby symbols carry no encoding

RB_UNUSED_VAR.caveat: CRuby marks a parameter or variable as unused (a compiler attribute); the name is kept and the attribute is dropped

RUBY_TYPED_FROZEN_SHAREABLE.caveat: mruby has no typed-data flags: free timing and the write-barrier flag are not represented; 0 keeps the initializer shape

rb_deprecate_constant.reason: CRuby warns when a deprecated constant is used; mruby has no constant deprecation, so the call has no effect

RB_OBJ_WRITE.caveat: the object must be a heap value (CRuby's RB_OBJ_WRITE has the same requirement); the write barrier is mruby's field barrier

StringValue.caveat: the argument is converted in place with to_str; the argument must be a plain identifier

RSTRING_END.caveat: the end of the string's bytes; the argument must be a plain identifier that is already a String (no to_str conversion)

RARRAY_CONST_PTR.caveat: mruby has no read-only element pointer: the same pointer as RARRAY_PTR, so writes through it are not refused

rb_obj_alloc.caveat: allocates a plain object of the class without calling initialize, as CRuby does; only plain-object instances: a class whose instances need a data type or string storage is not handled

TYPE.caveat: TYPE(x) is rb_type: it returns enum mrb_vtype, so compare only with MRB_TT_* values; nil and false both report MRB_TT_FALSE, so T_NIL and T_FALSE are refused

rb_yield.caveat: yields to the block the method was called with (fetched by the registered method's wrapper); only in a registered method's body: a helper has no block to yield to

rb_enc_str_new.caveat: the encoding argument is dropped: mruby strings carry no encoding, so the bytes are kept and the result is not tagged

rb_enc_associate.caveat: the encoding is dropped: mruby strings carry no encoding; the object is returned unchanged

rb_intern_const.caveat: argument must be a string literal (mrb_intern_lit is a macro over mrb_intern_static); a char pointer does not compile

rb_funcall.caveat: a literal argument count; the method name is rb_intern of a string literal or a character ID; the argument list is an mrb_value array (mrb_funcall_argv)

rb_hash_aset.caveat: mruby returns void; the CRuby return value (the stored value) is not available

rb_ary_push.caveat: mruby returns void; the CRuby return value (the array) is not available

RARRAY_AREF.caveat: CRuby reads the element pointer without a bounds check; mruby returns nil out of range and accepts negative offsets

rb_utf8_str_new.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and UTF-8 is not recorded

rb_obj_class.caveat: the struct RClass * is wrapped with mrb_obj_value: CRuby returns the class as a VALUE

rb_respond_to.caveat: returns mrb_bool (0 or 1), where CRuby returns int

rb_ivar_set.caveat: mruby returns void; the CRuby return value (the value) is not available

INT2FIX.caveat: no range check: the mruby fixnum range depends on the value boxing

LONG2FIX.caveat: no range check: the mruby fixnum range depends on the value boxing

FIX2INT.caveat: no check that the value is a fixnum; the result is mrb_int, not int

FIX2LONG.caveat: no check that the value is a fixnum; the result is mrb_int

rb_type.caveat: returns enum mrb_vtype: compare only with MRB_TT_* values. nil and false both report MRB_TT_FALSE (mruby/boxing_nan.h), so T_NIL and T_FALSE are not mapped

Qundef.caveat: mrb_value is a struct: test with mrb_undef_p(), not with ==

T_OBJECT.caveat: CRuby T_OBJECT also covers exception objects, which mruby types as MRB_TT_EXCEPTION (src/error.c:42); RB_TYPE_P and Check_Type do not match them, so T_OBJECT is refused in both

T_CLASS.caveat: mruby types singleton classes as MRB_TT_SCLASS (src/class.c:371) and CRuby reports them as T_CLASS, so T_CLASS is refused in both RB_TYPE_P and Check_Type

T_DATA.caveat: CRuby T_DATA also covers TypedData; MRB_TT_DATA is the nearest mruby C-data type, so check each use

rb_global_variable.caveat: needs the mruby fork's address roots (claude/gc-address-roots: mrb_gc_register_address reads *ptr at each collection); the value at the address stays rooted for as long as it is registered; CRuby's rb_global_variable never unregisters the address, and neither does this

rb_str_cat.caveat: the length is not checked for sign: a negative length becomes a large size_t

rb_str_buf_new.caveat: capa is a size hint only: the new string is empty, as in CRuby

rb_utf8_str_new_cstr.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and UTF-8 is not recorded

rb_str_freeze.caveat: mrb_obj_freeze freezes any object; CRuby's rb_str_freeze takes a String

rb_str_append.caveat: no encoding compatibility check (mruby has no encodings); CRuby raises Encoding::CompatibilityError for incompatible encodings

rb_ary_freeze.caveat: an array is an object: its freeze is mrb_obj_freeze (the same frozen flag)

rb_check_frozen.caveat: checks the object is not frozen; a value that is not a heap object raises in mruby's mrb_ptr

RHASH_SIZE.caveat: returns mrb_int (signed), where CRuby returns size_t

rb_ary_dup.reason: mrb_ary_dup is not in this fork; a copy is mrb_ary_new_from_values over the elements, which needs the RARRAY accessors by hand

NUM2DBL.caveat: a Float conversion through mruby's mrb_to_flo; a non-numeric value raises TypeError

rb_num2dbl.caveat: a Float conversion through mruby's mrb_to_flo; a non-numeric value raises TypeError

ULONG2NUM.caveat: mruby's Integer (mrb_fixnum_value); no range check: an unsigned value above the mrb_int maximum wraps negative

ULL2NUM.caveat: mruby's Integer (mrb_fixnum_value); no range check: an unsigned value above the mrb_int maximum wraps negative

NUM2LL.caveat: NUM2LL converts through mruby's integer conversion (mrb_to_int, the mrb_int macro): a Float is truncated, a non-numeric value raises TypeError

rb_id2name.caveat: the pointer is into mruby's symbol table: valid until the state is closed

rb_id2str.caveat: mruby does not promise a frozen result, as CRuby's rb_id2str does

rb_to_id.caveat: accepts only Symbol and String: CRuby also converts other objects with to_str

rb_isdigit.caveat: the C library ctype function in the C locale, which is ASCII-only as CRuby's ctype macros are

rb_isxdigit.caveat: the C library ctype function in the C locale, which is ASCII-only as CRuby's ctype macros are

rb_isspace.caveat: the C library ctype function in the C locale, which is ASCII-only as CRuby's ctype macros are

rb_isalpha.caveat: the C library ctype function in the C locale, which is ASCII-only as CRuby's ctype macros are

rb_isalnum.caveat: the C library ctype function in the C locale, which is ASCII-only as CRuby's ctype macros are

rb_isupper.caveat: the C library ctype function in the C locale, which is ASCII-only as CRuby's ctype macros are

rb_islower.caveat: the C library ctype function in the C locale, which is ASCII-only as CRuby's ctype macros are

rb_errinfo.caveat: mruby's mrb->exc is the exception being handled (nil when none); CRuby's $! is the same notion for a rescue body

rb_class_inherited_p.caveat: the fork's mrb_class_inherited_p (mrbgem-independent, src/class.c): true if the first class is the second or inherits or includes it, false if the second is a subclass of the first, nil if unrelated; both class arguments must be tracked class variables or RClass * expressions

rb_hash_bulk_insert.caveat: the fork's mrb_hash_bulk_insert (src/hash.c): argv holds argc elements, alternating keys and values, inserted in order as rb_hash_bulk_insert does

rb_apply.caveat: rb_apply(recv, mid, args) calls mid with the elements of the array args, as rb_funcallv does; the array is read, not retained

rb_reg_new.reason: stuck point: the fork has no Regexp class (no mruby-regexp mrbgem in mrbgems/) and no Regexp tag (include/mruby/value.h:106-131), so there is no regexp object to build or read

rb_reg_regcomp.reason: stuck point: the fork has no Regexp class (no mruby-regexp mrbgem in mrbgems/) and no Regexp tag (include/mruby/value.h:106-131), so there is no regexp object to build or read

RREGEXP_PTR.reason: stuck point: the fork has no Regexp class (no mruby-regexp mrbgem in mrbgems/) and no Regexp tag (include/mruby/value.h:106-131), so there is no regexp object to build or read

rb_block_given_p.caveat: the block slot of the current call frame (the fork's mrb_block_given_p, branch claude/block-given-p; mrb_get_args reads the same slot with &); it is false in a method called without a block

rb_const_defined.caveat: a module receiver does not fall back to Object, as in rb_const_get; returns mrb_bool

rb_const_defined_at.caveat: returns mrb_bool, where CRuby returns int

RB_LIKELY.caveat: the branch-prediction hint is dropped; !!(x) has the same 0 or 1 value as the GCC definition of RB_LIKELY

RB_UNLIKELY.caveat: the branch-prediction hint is dropped; !!(x) has the same 0 or 1 value as the GCC definition of RB_UNLIKELY

rb_class2name.caveat: CRuby first skips singleton and include classes (rb_class_real); mrb_class_name does not. An anonymous class gets a new name string, and the pointer into it can dangle after the next GC (a named class keeps its path string alive)

rb_define_alias.caveat: the class is a struct RClass * (as rb_undef_method): a class variable is passed unwrapped, and a VALUE there would not type-check. Names are C strings with the new name first (as in CRuby); the original must exist, as in CRuby (NameError)

rb_undef_method.caveat: the first argument is a struct RClass *, not a VALUE; a class variable there is passed unwrapped (special_arg_positions_class_only)

SYM2ID.caveat: no check that the value is a Symbol; the result is mrb_sym (the mapped type of ID), not an unsigned long

T_FALSE.caveat: mruby's nil also has type MRB_TT_FALSE (mrb_nil_p tells them apart by value), so this matches nil, which CRuby reports as T_NIL; RB_TYPE_P(x, T_FALSE) stays refused for this reason

RUBY_T_FIXNUM.caveat: mruby has no bignum, so MRB_TT_FIXNUM matches every Integer, including values CRuby reports as T_BIGNUM; RB_TYPE_P(x, T_FIXNUM) stays refused for this reason

T_FIXNUM.caveat: mruby has no bignum, so MRB_TT_FIXNUM matches every Integer, including values CRuby reports as T_BIGNUM; RB_TYPE_P(x, T_FIXNUM) stays refused for this reason

rb_eIndexError.caveat: struct RClass *, as E_ARGUMENT_ERROR: a VALUE use needs mrb_obj_value(); in rb_raise it is the class argument

rb_eRangeError.caveat: struct RClass *, as E_ARGUMENT_ERROR: a VALUE use needs mrb_obj_value(); in rb_raise it is the class argument

rb_warn.caveat: prints on every call; CRuby's rb_warn is silent when $VERBOSE is nil. Output is 'warning: ' and the message on stderr, with no file or line; PRIsVALUE is not supported

rb_sys_fail.caveat: raises SystemCallError (with the errno) only when mruby-errno defines it; otherwise RuntimeError with the message, which mruby does not allow to be NULL

rb_obj_classname.caveat: an anonymous class gets a new name string, and the pointer into it can dangle after the next GC (a named class keeps its path string alive), as for rb_class2name

rb_sym2id.caveat: no check that the value is a Symbol; the result is mrb_sym (the mapped type of ID), not an unsigned long

rb_warning.caveat: prints on every call: CRuby's rb_warning prints only in verbose mode ($VERBOSE true), and rb_warn always prints. Output is 'warning: ' and the message on stderr, with no file or line; PRIsVALUE is not supported

rb_gc_location.caveat: identity: mruby's collector never moves objects (no relocation API in include/ or src/gc.c), so the location is the value itself; the argument stays in parentheses

rb_str_buf_cat.caveat: CRuby's rb_str_buf_cat is an alias of rb_str_cat (ruby/internal/intern/string.h:1680); the length is not checked for sign: a negative length becomes a large size_t

rb_usascii_str_new.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and US-ASCII is not recorded

rb_usascii_str_new_cstr.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and US-ASCII is not recorded

rb_usascii_str_new2.caveat: CRuby's rb_usascii_str_new2 is an alias of rb_usascii_str_new_cstr (ruby/internal/intern/string.h:1679); mruby strings carry no encoding, so US-ASCII is not recorded

rb_ll2inum.caveat: mruby's Integer (mrb_fixnum_value); mrb_int may be narrower than long long: values outside its range are not preserved

NUM2UINT.caveat: NUM2UINT converts through mruby's integer conversion (mrb_to_int, the mrb_int macro): a Float is truncated, a non-numeric value raises TypeError

NUM2SIZET.caveat: NUM2SIZET converts through mruby's integer conversion (mrb_to_int, the mrb_int macro): a Float is truncated, a non-numeric value raises TypeError

FIX2ULONG.caveat: no check that the value is a fixnum; the result is mrb_int, not unsigned long

OBJ_FREEZE.caveat: CRuby's OBJ_FREEZE (rb_obj_freeze_inline, ruby/internal/fl_type.h:911) returns void; mruby's mrb_obj_freeze returns the object, which a statement use discards

rb_obj_is_kind_of.caveat: a condition (if/while, !, &&, ||) gets the mrb_bool; a value gets Qtrue/Qfalse; the class argument must be a tracked class variable or an RClass * expression

rb_obj_id.caveat: mruby's object id (mrb_int) is wrapped as an Integer VALUE; the numbers differ from CRuby's object_id, which only has to be stable and unique

CLASS_OF.caveat: the struct RClass * is wrapped with mrb_obj_value: CRuby's CLASS_OF returns a VALUE

rb_class_of.caveat: the struct RClass * is wrapped with mrb_obj_value: CRuby's rb_class_of returns a VALUE (ruby/internal/globals.h:174)

rb_include_module.caveat: both arguments are struct RClass * (class variables are passed unwrapped: special_arg_positions_class_only), so a VALUE class or module does not type-check; cyclic includes raise ArgumentError in both

rb_eFrozenError.caveat: struct RClass *, as E_ARGUMENT_ERROR: a VALUE use needs mrb_obj_value(); in rb_raise it is the class argument

RTYPEDDATA_DATA.caveat: both read the data field of a VALUE and are lvalues. mruby has no typed/untyped split: the object must be an mruby data object (mrb_data_type), and the type is not checked, as in CRuby

RB_INTEGER_TYPE_P.caveat: mruby has one fixnum tag (MRB_TT_FIXNUM): only a fixnum is an Integer here; a bignum-sized Integer has no mruby tag in this build

rb_define_private_method.caveat: registers a private method: the same wrapper and argument spec as rb_define_method (mrb_define_private_method has the same shape); the method is callable only without a receiver, as in CRuby

rb_iv_get.caveat: the name must be a string literal: it is interned with mrb_intern_cstr at each call; CRuby checks the name is an ivar name, mruby does not

rb_iv_set.caveat: the name must be a string literal: it is interned with mrb_intern_cstr at each call; CRuby checks the name is an ivar name, mruby does not

rb_protect.caveat: the function is called with the mruby state (mrb_func_t: mrb, then the data), so a callback passed here is threaded with an mrb argument (helper threading); the state argument is int * in CRuby but mrb_bool * in mruby, so a caller variable must be declared mrb_bool; only mruby exceptions are caught, and CRuby errinfo is not set

rb_class_new_instance.caveat: the arguments are reordered: CRuby rb_class_new_instance(argc, argv, klass) is mruby mrb_obj_new(mrb, klass, argc, argv); the class is a tracked class variable, a mapped class constant (rb_cRange is mrb->range_class), or a VALUE name or member unwrapped with mrb_class_ptr (CRuby requires a class there); argc may be an integer literal and argv NULL; both calls run initialize

rb_hash_lookup.caveat: returns nil when the key is missing (mrb_hash_fetch with a nil default), as CRuby does; the hash must be a Hash VALUE

rb_sym2str.caveat: the Symbol VALUE is converted with mrb_symbol; mruby does not promise a frozen result, as CRuby does

rb_cstr_to_inum.caveat: the C string becomes a String (mrb_str_new_cstr) and mrb_str_to_inum parses it; base and badcheck keep their order; the result is an Integer VALUE

rb_gv_get.caveat: the name must be a string literal: it is interned with mrb_intern_cstr at each call; special globals may behave differently in mruby

rb_gv_set.caveat: the name must be a string literal: it is interned with mrb_intern_cstr at each call; special globals may behave differently in mruby

rb_reg_nth_match.caveat: match[nth] on the OnigMatchData of the gem (api_map: onig regexp API), nil for a nil match, as CRuby does; the match is an OnigMatchData, not a MatchData

rb_backref_get.caveat: reads $~, which the onig gem sets when its @set_global_variables flag is on; otherwise it is nil

rb_backref_set.caveat: writes $~ (the onig gem reads it back through its last-match variable); the value is the match, as CRuby stores it

rb_match_busy.reason: a hint that keeps a match object from being reused; mruby has no match cache to keep, so the call has no effect

rb_jump_tag.caveat: re-raises the exception that mrb_protect caught (mrb->exc); CRuby's state argument is not needed, and the state is ignored

RUBY_TYPED_FREE_IMMEDIATELY.caveat: mruby has no typed-data flags: free timing and the write-barrier flag are not represented; 0 keeps the initializer shape

RUBY_TYPED_WB_PROTECTED.caveat: mruby has no typed-data flags: free timing and the write-barrier flag are not represented; 0 keeps the initializer shape

RUBY_TYPED_EMBEDDABLE.caveat: mruby has no typed-data flags: free timing and the write-barrier flag are not represented; 0 keeps the initializer shape

rb_data_typed_object_wrap.caveat: wraps the C pointer in a data object of the given mrb_data_type; the class must be a tracked class variable (struct RClass *)

TypedData_Wrap_Struct.caveat: CRuby TypedData_Wrap_Struct(klass, type, sval) reordered to mrb_data_object_alloc(mrb, klass, sval, type)

TypedData_Make_Struct.caveat: allocates a zeroed struct with mrb_calloc (freed by the type dfree), as CRuby does; the struct pointer is assigned to the last argument

TypedData_Get_Struct.caveat: reads the data pointer with mrb_data_get_ptr, which raises TypeError on a mismatched type, as CRuby does

rb_hash_foreach.caveat: the callback gets (mrb, key, value, void *): its third VALUE parameter is the pointer it is given; a callback result of 0 continues and non-zero breaks (ST_CONTINUE and ST_STOP); ST_DELETE is refused because mruby would break the loop on it

ST_CONTINUE.caveat: mrb_hash_foreach continues while the callback returns 0

ST_STOP.caveat: mrb_hash_foreach breaks on any non-zero result, so ST_STOP (1) stops the loop as in CRuby

RBIMPL_ATTR_NORETURN.reason: a no-return attribute: a hint for the compiler that mruby does not need; the declaration has the same meaning without it

rb_eIOError.caveat: IOError is defined by the mruby-io gem; mrb_exc_get raises at run time if it is not loaded

rb_eEOFError.caveat: EOFError is defined by the mruby-io gem

rb_eEncodingError.caveat: mruby has no encodings; the exception is only the class

rb_cFixnum.caveat: mruby has one Integer class; CRuby Fixnum and Bignum are both Integer here

rb_cFile.caveat: File is defined by the mruby-io gem

rb_cTime.caveat: Time is defined by the mruby-time gem

rb_cStruct.caveat: Struct is defined by the mruby-struct gem

rb_cRegexp.caveat: Regexp is defined by the mruby-onig-regexp gem

rb_cRandom.caveat: Random is defined by the mruby-random gem

rb_cRational.caveat: Rational is defined by a mruby gem

rb_gc_unregister_address.caveat: needs the mruby fork's address roots (claude/gc-address-roots: mrb_gc_register_address reads *ptr at each collection); the value at the address stays rooted for as long as it is registered

xmalloc.caveat: CRuby's allocator raises NoMemoryError on failure; mruby's raises RuntimeError

xcalloc.caveat: CRuby's allocator raises NoMemoryError on failure; mruby's raises RuntimeError

xrealloc.caveat: CRuby's allocator raises NoMemoryError on failure; mruby's raises RuntimeError

xfree.caveat: CRuby's allocator raises NoMemoryError on failure; mruby's raises RuntimeError

ruby_xmalloc.caveat: CRuby's allocator raises NoMemoryError on failure; mruby's raises RuntimeError

ruby_xcalloc.caveat: CRuby's allocator raises NoMemoryError on failure; mruby's raises RuntimeError

ruby_xrealloc.caveat: CRuby's allocator raises NoMemoryError on failure; mruby's raises RuntimeError

ruby_xfree.caveat: CRuby's allocator raises NoMemoryError on failure; mruby's raises RuntimeError

rb_str_cat2.caveat: appends the NUL-terminated bytes; returns the string, as CRuby

rb_str_cat_cstr.caveat: appends the NUL-terminated bytes; returns the string, as CRuby

rb_undef_alloc_func.caveat: mruby has no separate allocator: the class's new is undefined, so Klass.new raises NoMethodError where CRuby raises TypeError (allocator undefined); the argument must be a tracked class variable

RB_OBJ_WRITTEN.caveat: the object must be a heap value; the old value is not needed by mruby's field barrier, as CRuby's write barrier does not need it

SSIZET2NUM.caveat: CRuby's Integer from a C size (signed for SSIZET2NUM): mruby's fixnum; a value beyond mruby's integer range is not represented

SIZET2NUM.caveat: CRuby's Integer from a C size (signed for SSIZET2NUM): mruby's fixnum; a value beyond mruby's integer range is not represented

rb_const_set.caveat: the class is a VALUE here (mrb_const_set takes an mrb_value); the ID is an mrb_sym

rb_class_name.caveat: returns the class name as a String (CRuby returns a VALUE); the argument is a class value

rb_id2sym.caveat: an ID is an mrb_sym here; the Symbol value is mrb_symbol_value

rb_intern2.caveat: interns the bytes (length given), as CRuby's rb_intern2

rb_mEnumerable.caveat: Enumerable is a mruby gem module (mruby-enumerator); looked up by name, raises at run time if the gem is not loaded

rb_mComparable.caveat: Comparable is looked up by name, as Enumerable

rb_str_concat.caveat: appends the other value to the string and returns the string, as CRuby's rb_str_concat

RB_OBJ_FREEZE.caveat: freezes the object; the result is not used (CRuby's RB_OBJ_FREEZE is void)

LL2NUM.caveat: an mruby fixnum; a value beyond mruby's integer range is not represented

NUM2SSIZET.caveat: converts through mruby's integer conversion (see NUM2INT)

NUM2USHORT.caveat: converts through mruby's integer conversion (see NUM2INT)

NUM2ULL.caveat: converts through mruby's integer conversion (see NUM2INT)

rb_bug.caveat: the format is printed by mruby's formatter; CRuby's PRIsVALUE arguments are not mapped (refused where they appear)

rb_sprintf.caveat: returns a String built by mruby's formatter (see rb_bug for the format); PRIsVALUE in the format becomes %S (%!S for the + flag)

rb_ary_new_from_values.caveat: copies the n values into a new Array, as CRuby's rb_ary_new_from_values

FIXNUM_MAX.caveat: CRuby's FIXNUM_MAX (2^62-1 on 64-bit): the value is kept, so the converted code makes the same Fixnum/Bignum decisions; the mruby integer is wider, so a value in this range is still an mruby fixnum

FIXNUM_MIN.caveat: CRuby's FIXNUM_MIN (-2^62 on 64-bit): the value is kept (see FIXNUM_MAX)

rb_rational_new2.caveat: needs the mruby-rational gem (its Kernel#Rational and Rational#numerator / denominator); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

rb_rational_new.caveat: needs the mruby-rational gem (its Kernel#Rational and Rational#numerator / denominator); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

rb_Rational.caveat: needs the mruby-rational gem (its Kernel#Rational and Rational#numerator / denominator); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

rb_rational_new1.caveat: needs the mruby-rational gem (its Kernel#Rational and Rational#numerator / denominator); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

rb_Rational1.caveat: needs the mruby-rational gem (its Kernel#Rational and Rational#numerator / denominator); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

rb_rational_num.caveat: needs the mruby-rational gem (its Kernel#Rational and Rational#numerator / denominator); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

rb_rational_den.caveat: needs the mruby-rational gem (its Kernel#Rational and Rational#numerator / denominator); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

rb_struct_aref.caveat: needs the mruby-struct gem (Struct#[] and Struct#size); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

RSTRUCT_GET.caveat: needs the mruby-struct gem (Struct#[]); the index is a C integer here (CRuby's RSTRUCT_GET takes a long), so it is converted to an Integer value

RSTRUCT_LEN.caveat: needs the mruby-struct gem (Struct#[] and Struct#size); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build; the length is an mrb_int (as CRuby's long)

rb_time_nano_new.caveat: needs the mruby-time gem (Time.at); mruby's Time keeps microseconds, so the nanoseconds are divided by 1000 (the sub-microsecond part is dropped)

rb_time_new.caveat: needs the mruby-time gem (Time.at with seconds and microseconds, as CRuby's rb_time_new)

rb_enc_interned_str.caveat: the encoding argument is dropped (mruby strings carry no encoding): the bytes are kept; CRuby's interned string is frozen, this one is not

rb_enc_str_asciicompat_p.caveat: mruby strings are byte strings with no encoding, so every string is taken as ASCII-compatible; a CRuby string in a non-ASCII-compatible encoding (UTF-16) has no mruby form

rb_obj_method_arity.caveat: needs the mruby-method gem (Object#method and Method#arity); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build; the arity is a C int (CRuby's rb_obj_method_arity returns int)

rb_big2str.caveat: calls to_s with the base (Integer#to_s), as CRuby's rb_big2str

rb_cstr2inum.caveat: parses the C string in the base without the badcheck (CRuby's rb_cstr2inum with badcheck off)

ST2FIX.caveat: a st_data_t / st_index_t value is a fixnum here (as INT2FIX); the value must fit mruby's integer

rb_io_write.caveat: calls write on the IO (mruby-io), as CRuby's rb_io_write

rb_enc_copy.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding, so copying one's encoding to another does nothing

rb_must_asciicompat.caveat: every mruby string is ASCII-compatible (see rb_enc_str_asciicompat_p), so the check always passes

rb_ary_new3.caveat: a literal count; the values are an mrb_value array (mrb_ary_new_from_values)

rb_to_int.caveat: converts the value to an Integer (to_int), as CRuby's rb_to_int

rb_exc_new2.caveat: a new exception of the class with the message (CRuby's rb_exc_new2); the class must be a tracked class variable

rb_yield_values2.caveat: yields the argc values of argv to the block (as rb_yield_values2); valid only in a registered method (the block is fetched by its wrapper)

rb_check_typeddata.caveat: checks the value's data type and returns its pointer (mruby's mrb_data_get_ptr raises on another type), as CRuby's rb_check_typeddata

rb_obj_call_init.caveat: calls initialize on the object with argc values from argv (CRuby's rb_obj_call_init)

rb_int_positive_pow.caveat: x ** y on Integers (Integer#**), as CRuby's rb_int_positive_pow

rb_struct_s_members.caveat: the struct class's members (mruby-struct's Struct.members), as CRuby's rb_struct_s_members; needs the struct gem

RB_ALLOC.caveat: allocates the bytes with mrb_malloc (raises on failure, as CRuby's xmalloc raises NoMemoryError); the pointer is void * as in CRuby

RB_ALLOC_N.caveat: n values of the type, allocated with mrb_malloc (see RB_ALLOC)

RB_REALLOC_N.caveat: reallocates the variable to n values of the type with mrb_realloc (see RB_ALLOC_N)

rb_gc.caveat: a full collection, as CRuby's rb_gc

rb_hash.caveat: calls hash on the object (Object#hash), as CRuby's rb_hash

rb_singleton_class.caveat: the singleton class of the value, as CRuby's rb_singleton_class (returns a VALUE in both)

rb_alias.caveat: aliases the method of the class (the class must be a tracked class variable; the names are IDs, mrb_sym here)

rb_str_to_inum.caveat: parses the string in the base; badcheck as given (CRuby's rb_str_to_inum)

RB_FLOAT_TYPE_P.caveat: a Float test (mruby's float tag), as CRuby's RB_FLOAT_TYPE_P

rb_special_const_p.caveat: an immediate value (no heap object), as CRuby's special constant test (the immediates differ: mruby's are not CRuby's)

RSTRING_GETMEM.caveat: the pointer and length of the string, as CRuby's RSTRING_GETMEM
